progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: From B6b: the template strand is paired (A with U, T with A, C with G, G with C) to build mRNA; the coding strand matches the mRNA with U for T; mRNA runs 5' to 3'. From B6c: the codon chart is read with mRNA codons; AUG is the start codon; stop codons add no amino acid. From b03: substitution, insertion, deletion; silent, missense, nonsense; a frameshift when the number of bases added or removed is not a multiple of three. From b04: deletion, duplication, inversion, translocation; balanced rearrangements keep every gene; nondisjunction in meiosis gives a gamete with an extra or missing chromosome. From b05: somatic mutations are copied by mitosis into one cell's descendants and are not inherited in animals; germ-line mutations can be. Not assumed: monosomy as a term (glossed in Q3 as "one chromosome missing"), myostatin (glossed in the stem).
progression.startsWith: An unfamiliar mutated sequence, chromosome, karyotype or case with a hidden trap. The video opens: Mutation questions in the HSC give you something to read, a DNA sequence, a chromosome diagram, a karyotype or a case.
progression.stopsAfter: writing mRNA from a template strand and classifying three substitutions as silent, nonsense and missense with their effects; aligning a mutant sequence base by base to find a deletion and an insertion, and explaining why the frame is restored after the second change; naming an inversion that includes the centromere and explaining why it is not a translocation; explaining how a 45,X karyotype can arise by nondisjunction of the sex chromosomes; explaining why an 11-base deletion gives a non-functional protein, and why the same deletion in one body cell of a cow cannot be inherited by her calves.
progression.nextLesson: how meiosis and fertilisation vary offspring (route entry bio-m6-b07).

teaching.task: When a question hands you a mutated sequence, chromosome or case you've never seen, how do you work out what changed, what it does, and who can inherit it?
teaching.causalExplanation: Why the mRNA is a pairing, not a copy, of the template (2b); why each mutant has its effect (the new codon on the chart, 2c); why a stop ends the chain (2c); why codons 2 to 5 change (the deletion shifts the frame, 3c) and why 6 and 7 do not (one removed, one added, 3c); why the diagram shows an inversion and not a translocation (same genes, same chromosome, 4b, 4d); how 45,X arises (sex chromosomes fail to separate in one parent's meiosis, 4c); why 11 bases give no working myostatin (not a multiple of three, frameshift, early stop, missing active end, 5b); why the cow's calves cannot inherit it (somatic, copied only by mitosis, not in her eggs, 5c).
teaching.conversationalApproach: A hard-practice walkthrough (the walkthroughs are the content): four HSC-style questions written for HSCScience, each shown with its full exam wording, a protected 10 second attempt, then one reasoning stage per scene with each given underlined in the question strip as it is used, and one crossed-out classic mistake. Q1 pairs a template strand to mRNA and compares three mutants one triplet at a time; Q2 aligns a mutant base by base and explains why the frame is restored after the second change; Q3 names an inversion that includes the centromere and explains how 45,X can arise by nondisjunction; Q4 explains why an 11-base deletion gives a non-functional myostatin and why the same deletion in one muscle cell cannot be inherited. The decision board collects the first move for each kind of question and hands off to b07.
teaching.openingDecision: Mutation questions in the HSC give you something to read, a DNA sequence, a chromosome diagram, a karyotype or a case. Every one comes down to three checks. What changed, base by base or gene by gene? What does it do, to the codons, the frame, or the genes? And who can inherit it? Here are four HSC-style questions. Pause and try each one, then we'll work it through, one step at a time.
teaching.understandingCheck: Four, each 10 s with the countdown and every demand and condition visible (2a, 3a, 4a, 5a). Nothing answer-bearing during the holds; the check strip dims.
teaching.curriculumScope: B6-IQ1-02 "compare the causes, processes and effects of different types of mutation, including but not limited to:" with "point mutation" and "chromosomal mutation" (Q1 to Q4); B6-IQ1-03 "distinguish between somatic mutations and germ-line mutations and their effect on an organism   (ACSBL082, ACSBL083)" (Q4 part b). Practice and transfer only: the ledger rows stay with b03, b04 and b05; G01 adds a practice row, not first coverage. The three spaces before "(ACSBL082" are in the official DOCX extraction and are kept verbatim in the YouTube block.

design.visualSystem: One practice board throughout, in the G03c layout, updated for the worded-question rule: top-left the question card (stem, data and demands, as an exam prints them, with the "HSC-style question, written for HSCScience" tag), kept readable through the whole question; the working fills the right two thirds; a type badge top-right ("Point mutations", "Frameshift", "Chromosomes", "Effect and inheritance"), hidden during each attempt where it would name the answer. When the walkthrough starts, the card shrinks to a strip and each given is underlined in amber in the question text at the cue where it is used (no givens card). A check strip on the far left carries three rows, "what changed?", "what does it do?", "who inherits it?", and ticks the row each scene uses; it dims to an outline during every countdown. Earlier questions are cleared before the next card writes on. Sequences: typeset text in a fixed-width face, codons spaced in threes, DNA in ink on a slim baseline (b01 `SlimStrand` look, two thin lines, at reduced height), mRNA in terracotta (B6b); no letter tiles. Chromosomes: b04's HSC-style `GeneBar` (long rounded bar with a narrowed centromere, cream fill, ink outline, gene letters beside thin bands). Karyotype: b04's coded karyotype strip (B9 look). Real objects are painted: the T4 phage (new plate), the Belgian Blue bull (new plate) and the red cow (`m5x-cattle-red-v1.png`). No people. Clutter rule (owner, 19 Oct): besides the question strip and the check strip, at most about three bright text items in the working area at once; each working tag fades when the next cue lands.
design.transitionPlan: One practice board persists: the question card writes on at the top left with the HSC-style tag, the check strip on the far left dims during each countdown and ticks its row as each scene uses it; each walkthrough shrinks the card to a strip with the type badge and adds one reasoning stage at a time in the working area (codon rows, alignment rows, gene bars, karyotype strip, cell tree), each tag fading as the next cue lands; each mistake scene writes a chip and crosses it; earlier questions clear before the next card writes on; the check strip grows into the two-column decision board, and the next chip slides in; scene crossfade with settle.
